title: run-hang-guarded hardening from the #662 review: settle on exit, sample budget, attempt-2 margin, behavioural pins
description:
Follow-up carrying findings 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the LCLI-760 review (verdict recorded verbatim on LCLI-760). Nothing here is started; it waits for plan approval.
1 (MEDIUM, leads): scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs settles on `close`, which waits for the stdio pipes to reach EOF, not on `exit`. If bun exits on its own but a leaked grandchild still holds stdout or stderr, `close` never fires, the watchdog sees silence after 120 s and the guard exits 124; ci.yml retries on 124 without reading the log, so a real failure becomes a retry and a flaky one becomes RETRY-GREEN. Suggested fix: record the child's `exit` code and, on `exit`, give the pipes a short grace period before settling with that code.
2 (LOW): the '<=150 s detect + sample + kill' budget assumes few bun processes; sampleGroup runs `sample pid 3` serially with spawnSync and a 60 s cap each, so N buns cost at least 3N seconds and block the event loop. How many buns --isolate leaves in the group is not measured for the real suite.
4 (LOW): SECONDS counts only from the start of the Test step, and the classifier path has a corner case: if attempt 1 takes ~579 s then fails with all-hangs, attempt 2 gets ~521 s, and a healthy attempt 2 near 579 s is killed at 125 and the job goes red. The ci.yml comment 'even the classifier arm cannot run into the job timeout' is true by construction, not by margin.
5 (LOW): the ci-workflow.test.ts pins are presence checks on workflow text: a changed `elif` condition or an edited body of the 125 branch still passes, and `timeout 5 bun test` or `env bun test` would not trip the bare-invocation check. Make them behavioural or anchor them to the branch structure.
